Vesper tucks the key safely into her satchel and drops her voice to a whisper. "Thank you for the quiet, big fellow, I'll try not to wake you." She wades into the Keepers' gallery, keeping the lamp's gold at her back, and follows the river air up toward the Water-Stair to catch Odalie and find the Reeve before Ashgrove thinks to circle the hill.

"DM: when I get out, can I still hear the bell in town, and is Brannoc Vell's watch answering it yet?"

entries.text:
The gallery is a cold, low crawl. The water is ankle-deep and so cold it aches, and the lamp's gold fades behind you until your darkvision turns the tunnel to grey. The Sleeper's breathing follows you a long way, slow and enormous, then dies into the drip of water.

You come out at the landing under the carved lantern arch, where the Water-Stair spirals down toward Eel Row. Here the hill's stone carries sound well. As you climb down, you hear the bell. It's faint and has stopped now, as if someone cut the rope, but its last strokes are still ringing in the walls. Under it, thinner and farther off, a second sound answers: the harbour horn at the Grand Quay, three long notes, then three more. It's the Reeve's call for the watch.

So he is stirring, but he isn't at the hill yet. Through the stone you also catch the clatter of boots on the cobbles above, men running the other way around the hill to head off the stair, and a voice you now know calling, "Round the back, the net-sheds!" Ashgrove has thought to circle it.

One more thing, as the DM: your sheet now shows you at level 2 with 15 maximum hit points and a "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin" in your pack, and no rapier. I have no record in my notes of Garrow Quill or that pin, so tell me what you know of them. Carry on from here as if the sheet is right.

You have perhaps a minute on the stair before the net-sheds fill with raiders. Odalie, Mags and Tamsin are down there too.

The gallery is ankle-deep and cold, and the lamp's gold fades behind you until your darkvision takes over. The water runs against you, whispering over old stone, and the dripping of the Water-Stair grows louder with every turn. Behind you, muffled by the hill and the iron door, comes the dull thud of the ram. It's slower now. Ashgrove has stopped hurrying.

To answer your question as the DM: no, you can't hear the bell any more. You stopped ringing it, and the echo died minutes ago. But when the gallery opens onto the landing under the carved lantern arch, the night comes down the stair with cold air and river smell, and with it a sound from the town below. It's a horn, long and flat, blown twice from the Grand Quay, then a third time nearer. Lanterns are moving in the lower streets, and a few dozen voices are shouting. Somebody has answered the bell, though you can't tell whether it's the Reeve's watch or only frightened townsfolk.

Ten minutes of wading brings you out onto the landing. At the far end of the stair, in the dark, a small shape sits on the bottom step with her habit hitched to her knees and her breath coming hard. Odalie hasn't made it down. She's waiting. When she sees your face, still half in her own features, she gives a dry, shaky laugh.

"I couldn't leave you to climb out alone," she says. "Foolish old woman. Help me down, child, and let's find that Reeve."

Below, the lane behind the net-sheds is quiet for now, and Mags's door is fifty yards off. The horn blows again from the quay.

Vesper lets the disguise drop with a rueful laugh, raises both hands, and steps lightly onto the barrels as if she'd planned it. "Well, Captain, you've caught me being predictable. A kettle is the first honest thing anyone's offered me tonight, and I'd hate to waste it."

A note from me as DM before the scene continues: your sheet has changed in ways I never made in play. It now shows level 2 hit dice, 15 max HP and 425 XP, 0 of 3 spell slots, no rapier, a brass lantern key in your pack, and an item called "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin". I'll run the scene from what was actually played, and the key stays Ashgrove's unless you tell me what happened. If the sheet is wrong, tell me and I'll correct it.

The disguise falls from your face. Your hands are up, and you step onto the barrels as if you'd planned it. The sentry's crossbow follows you, a steady black line, and his eyes dart to the cabin for orders.

Ashgrove laughs, a short real laugh, the first you've heard from her. "Oh, I do like her. Yes, bring your cup, Miss Thorne. Garrick, lower that. If she wanted a fight, she'd have come with more than a kettle's worth of nerve." The white glove beckons. "Leave the rapier at the door, as a courtesy. line:
Vesper lets the disguise drop with a rueful laugh, raises both hands, and steps lightly onto the barrels as if she'd planned it. "Well, Captain, you've caught me being predictable. A kettle is the first honest thing anyone's offered me tonight, and I'd hate to waste it."

She keeps her tail tucked and her eyes on the cabin door while she signals Ysolt with two slow fingers down by her hip: *wait.* "Mind if I bring my own cup? I'd like to hear what a woman with half the words offers for the other half."

entries.text:
Ashgrove's smile widens a little. "A cup of your own. Of course. Bring it, and your hands where Harl can see them."

The sentry's crossbow follows you up the gangplank. The hulk's boards are soft with rot and smell of tar and cold tea. Inside the cabin a stove ticks, a table is laid for two, and your satchel sits unopened beside the teapot with its flap buckled. Ashgrove lowers herself into the better chair and pours without looking at you. Two more raiders hold the door. Through the cabin's one shuttered port you can just make out the reeds on the far bank, where Ysolt waits on your signal.

"Half the words," she says, as if tasting the phrase. "You're quick. I was told you were a thief, and thieves don't usually think in halves."

Level up! New spell: Healing Word, since I've nearly died once already and a heal at range beats a prayer. No swaps, and I'll take the fixed 6 hit points, because I don't trust my luck with a d8 after that natural 1 at the hulk.

Then she holds up the key to the lantern light. "Corvin, drop us at Tanner's Stair by dawn. Ashgrove means to open the Weeping Locks at the new moon and drown the lower town, so I need Odalie, the Reeve, and a way to break that lock before then."

When you reach it, you'll choose a bard college, two expertise skills, three bonus skills and a new spell.

Two things on the sheet to flag. Your rapier is gone: the sentry took it off the barrel at the hulk, so for now you have the dagger. You also carry "Garrow Quill's half of the sluice-pin," which is the iron pin that was stuck through the Weeping Locks on Ashgrove's chart. Quill is the lock-keeper there, and the flood-gates can't be opened without his half.

The *Plump Heron* slides into Tanner's Stair at dawn, grey and cold. You've slept a few hours between the bales, and your HP is mostly back, but your spell slots will need a proper long rest. Odalie is waiting on the steps in a borrowed shawl with Brannoc Vell, Ysolt (who rowed ahead) and Tamsin leaning on a crutch. You hold up the key and the pin.

"Seven nights to the new moon," the Reeve says. "The Locks are a day's ride upriver. I can raise a dozen watchmen, no more. Garrow Quill has kept those gates for thirty years and I'd have sworn on my own wife's grave he's honest."

Odalie looks at the pin. "Then someone is holding his family, or his debts," she says.

sheet.name: Vesper Thorne
sheet.opening: Vesper Thorne, a violet-skinned tiefling bard and con artist (chaotic neutral, CHA 17, rapier, lute, Sleep, Charm Person, Disguise Self, Faerie Fire, Vicious Mockery, Minor Illusion), is a level-1 character. Backstory (must stay true): found as a toddler in a fish crate on the steps of the shabby Shrine of the Lantern Saint in the river town of Marrowmere; raised by overworked Sister Odalie, who taught her scripture and never quite caught her stealing, and who gave her her first silk scarf (Vesper keeps that scarf in her pack always, never parted with, even while wearing newer scarves over her curling horns). Vesper worked the pews on feast days, then market stalls. At sixteen she left in the night with the shrine's silver offering bowl, never sold it, still carries it polished in her pack, and means to return it someday; the debt to Odalie is bigger than the bowl. Ideal: freedom, no one writes her script. Flaw: cannot resist a mark too sure of themselves even when walking away is smarter. Her tail twitches when she lies so she keeps it tucked under her coat; gold eyes look too honest. She never tells the same story twice and will cheat anyone but never a friend. Carries 15 gp, leather armor, rapier, dagger, lute, a stolen reliquary bearing another faith's saint, an annotated prayer book. Opening suggestion: Vesper is on the road some days from Marrowmere, arriving at the river-crossing village of Hollin Ford at dusk, mid-con, working a loud, overconfident merchant (exactly the kind of mark she can't resist) at the ferry inn with a fake relic story, when a wounded courier stumbles in clutching a sealed satchel and a message that names the Shrine of the Lantern Saint, or news arrives that Marrowmere's river shrine is in trouble. Something has just happened that pulls both her con and her unpaid debt to Odalie into the story, and forces her to choose between cheating the mark and acting.
